programme.title: MeatEater
programme.desc: Steven Rinella takes to the canyons of the West Texas desert in search of javelina. In this broken, rocky terrain finding these unique critters isn't easy and getting a clear shot on a skunk pig with a bow is a whole other story. But Steve is inspired by the evidence of he finds of ancient hunters that used the area to prepare a meal that honors both the animal and our hunting ancestors.

programme.title: MeatEater

programme.title: MeatEater
programme.desc: Steven Rinella is on New Zealand's South Island for a do-it-yourself, free-range hunt for the majestic red stag. But first, he needs to secure some camp meat in the form of wild lamb. Battling weather and wary game in mountainous terrain, he uses his spot-and-stalk hunting skills to discover Kiwi red stags are a trophy worthy of the wall and the cook pot.

programme.title: MeatEater
programme.desc: Steven Rinella and local pig hunting expert, Darren Moore, spend a wild, action-packed day tracking down Captain Cook boars in the thick New Zealand bush. Their tools for the job include two tough little pig dogs, a knife, and some real grit. Wild pigs are dangerous critters and this is as visceral as a hunt gets. Along the way, Steve learns a new technique for field-prepping whole hogs.

programme.title: MeatEater
programme.desc: With the help of guide and friend Remi Warren, Steven Rinella gears up for a massive climb into New Zealand's Southern Alps in pursuit of Chamois and Tahr. The hunters will travel light and base out of an alpine hut to find animals Steve has never hunted. Things turns adventurous quickly; with an impassable glacial river between Steve and his goal. But with hard work, Steve experiences a do-it-yourself high country hunt like no other.

programme.title: MeatEater
programme.desc: Steven Rinella and special guest, the author Tim Ferriss, travel to the remote north slope of Alaska.

programme.title: MeatEater
programme.desc: After drawing one of the most coveted big game tags in North America, a Tok Management Area Dall sheep tag, Steven Rinella heads out for a truly rare and epic Alaskan experience. Along with his brother Danny and friend Paul, Steve is dropped deep into the Alaska Range. After a rugged hike through nasty weather, Steve's skills and fortitude are tested against his elusive, high-climbing quarry.

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.desc: Steven Rinella talks with John Carter and Randall Williams. Topics discussed: The history of hot dogs; the science of meat emulsions; characteristics of the perfect hot dog; what goes into the dogs; clean factories; skinless casings; the importance of salt and ice; why it's so tough to make a good wild game hot dog; and more.

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.desc: Steven Rinella talks with Caleb Hubbard of the Hubbard Urban Entymology Lab at New Mexico State University and "Bubbly" Doug Duren. Topics discussed: Stay tuned for twice a week MeatEater Podcast drops starting in March; come to the Safari Club International 2026 Convention on Feb. 19th to see Steve and Morgan Potter; a correction on Colorado wolf recovery; sous vide rewarming for frostbite; the ins and outs of the New World screw worm; how all warm blooded critters are potential hosts; being eaten alive; Doug's Sharing the Land organization; and more. The New World Screwworm Threat Survey: https://acesnmsu.az1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eLjo05717Wzz1em The New World Screwworm is a serious pest threat to livestock and wildlife, and New Mexico is taking steps to stay proactive-not reactive. The survey gathers input from ranchers, producers, hunters, land stewards, and community members across New Mexico. We're studying what people know, believe, and need regarding screwworm prevention and response.

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.desc: Steven Rinella and the MeatEater crew discuss: Steve's new baby mouse; Corner Crossing updates; the endangered jaguar hanging out in Arizona; live sonar for billfish and the end of integrity in fishing; Louisiana's National Forest land transfer; the first ever detection of CWD in Wyoming's largest elk herd; South Dakota sets an unprecedented elk hunting management plan; Michigan's major buck hunting rule changes; and more.

programme.title: The MeatEater Podcast
programme.desc: Steven Rinella talks with New Mexico Senator Martin Heinrich, Ryan Callaghan, and Randall Williams. Topics discussed: Corner crossing and the Supreme Court ruling; stream access; the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge, mining, and caribou; the Roadless Rule; where to develop and not develop renewables; relative bipartisan support for nuclear energy; reintroducing pronghorn back to an area of New Mexico; the breadth of the coalition that came together around keeping public lands in public hands; and more.

programme.title: Runaway Country with Alex Wagner
programme.desc: As ballots start coming in, an increasingly desperate president is already meddling in the vote count. Alex sits down with Chris Hayes, host of MS NOW’s “All In” to talk about the Alaska fiasco, how the media should be covering threats to democracy, and what might be waiting for us on the other side of Election Day. But first, how are state election officials responding to threats from the federal government? Journalist and author Barton Gellman has been reporting from the frontlines, and he comes on the show to share what, specifically, elections officials are worried about…and how they’re preparing for Tuesday.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.desc: We’re in the final stretch before Election Day, with early voting underway and new polls still rolling in. The latest CNN poll shows Kansas Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Adam Hamilton leading Republican Senator Roger Marshall by four points. On today’s show, Jane speaks with Hamilton, a pastor-turned-candidate, about what he would bring to the state, where rural hospitals face some of the highest risks of closure in the country.

programme.title: Hysteria
programme.desc: Erin and MS Now’s Ali Vitali check in on Trump’s midterm rally tour, discuss the potential future a Democratic majority could bring, and unpack Marissa Mayer’s effort to sell moms on her AI assistants. They wrap it up in the sanity corner with a toast to the late Dolores Huerta.

programme.title: Lovett or Leave It
programme.desc: Gas prices go up, Ukraine’s Starlink goes down, and Ilhan Omar is caught in the middle. This week, Ben Feldman of Ghosts and Superstore talks Netflix fame, the French-Canadian language police, and being a dirty little trailer pig (?), while Dusty Slay opens up about drag queens, ghost writers and private drawings. We shake our fist at costume parties, tiny plates and visiting L.A. for The Rant Wheel, and take our time saying farewell with Second Thoughts.

programme.title: What a Day
programme.desc: This weekend, Senator Bernie Sanders will rally with Florida Democratic State Representative Angie Nixon, who is challenging Republican Senator Ashley Moody for Florida's U.S. Senate seat. Running on a platform of lowering costs, raising wages, and putting everyday people first, Nixon joins Jane to discuss her campaign.

programme.title: Offline with Jon Favreau
programme.desc: What would you do if your son texted you in the middle of the night that he'd stumbled upon a bizarre castle lorded over by a creepy man? For Jon Ronson, the journalist and bestselling author of So You've Been Publicly Shamed and The Psychopath Test, the answer is simple: write a book about it. The Castle: Adventures in a World of Unraveling Men is an empathetic, humorous, and startling investigation of men who are struggling to find purpose, connection, and place in a rapidly changing world. Jon and Jon talk about what happened to the institutions that once gave people a sense of belonging, how the internet has offered new—and sometimes dangerous—substitutes, and what all of this means for raising boys.

programme.title: What a Day

Running on a platform of lowering costs, raising wages, and putting everyday people first, Nixon joins Jane to discuss her campaign.

programme.title: Pod Save America
programme.desc: Trump makes the case for Jon Husted in Ohio, praising the Republican senator's greatest asset: his athletic behind. Jon and Dan react to Trump's Ohio rally and his other messages to voters on the campaign trail, Politico reporting that Trump is considering replacing White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles with an MLB executive, and new press secretary Katie Zacharia's brutal debut briefing. They discuss the president canceling the Department of Defense's plans to livestream the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan, the administration's deeply troubling attempt to strip Congresswoman Ilhan Omar of her citizenship, and another pathetic attempt at humor from Vice President JD Vance. Then, Sherrod Brown talks to Dan about his bid to retake his old Senate seat in the Buckeye State.

programme.desc: A day of hilarity and hysteria dawns on Capt. Miller and his men when they look for the kidnapper of an antique doll; a man is conned out of $500 for a confirmed reservation on the space shuttle, and Inspector Von Luger tells Barney that he is leaving him a $250,000 estate.

programme.title: Barney Miller
programme.desc: Comedy clicks like a Geiger counter when an agitated woman with a homemade pressure-cooker bomb threatens to blow up the squad room; the verdict in Harris' libel suit is finally reached, and retired Detective Fish makes a surprise visit.

programme.title: Barney Miller
programme.desc: When Inspector Luger tries to mollify a militant crowd of Hassidics, a demonstration turns into a riot, but Barney isn't ready to give up on society yet.

programme.title: Barney Miller
programme.desc: Chaos prevails at the 12th Precinct with the arrival of the detective's bulletproof vests and on an urgent call that someone is barricaded themselves in an apartment with two shotguns.

programme.title: Barney Miller
programme.desc: As Barney struggles with the fact that his men want to leave for promotions at another precinct, the squad gets a laugh out of a self-proclaimed rainmaker who is arrested while attempting to end New York's drought.

programme.title: Barney Miller
programme.desc: Sgt. Harris faces instant poverty when the court rules against him, and Dietrich helps a humble news dealer with a grievance against a multi-national corporation.

programme.title: Barney Miller
programme.desc: It's morning in the 12th Precinct squad room and Sgt. Harris is taking a statement from pretty Wendy McWilliams, who is in New York for a beauty contest. Her purse has been snatched and Harris sets her to work with the mug books. Meanwhile, Barney and Dietrich are discussing the Solidarity Movement and so on, but Wojehowicz, who might be expected to take an interest in the matter, just sits and broods. He explains he's been hit with a paternity suit, although he's having difficulty recalling the purported mother. It seems he has to have a blood test, so he leaves to see a doctor. Harris and Dietrich respond to a disturbance call from the Tivoli Theatre and return with Arthur Frane, who has just ruined a print of a horror film. Frane was offended by the subject matter. When Wojo returns from the doctor, he claims he's off the hook on the paternity charge. That's the good news. The bad news is that he's sterile and claims his sex life is over. Barney is unable to reassure him, but there isn't time anyway. Dietrich and Wojo are summoned to a warehouse burglary. When they return, Dietrich is shaken because Wojo went berserk, subdued an armed gunman without waiting for backup, and is apparently out to reestablish his manhood. Barney admonishes Wojo, but is unable to get through to him just now. Victor Lupton, who owns the Tivoli Theatre, arrives to swear out his complaint against Frane, but he's strangely reluctant. He admits that the film was terrible, but is basically too nice to press charges. In the meantime, Wendy has drawn a blank from the mug books and realizes she is stranded in New York with no money and no place to stay. While Barney is working out a compromise between Lupton and Frane, Wojo and Wendy strike up a conversation. Of course, she knows what is going on, and is sympathetic. He, on his part, offers her dinner. She sees it as a challenge and accepts. As the others make graceful exits, Wojo and Wendy plan their evening together.

programme.title: Sortilegio
programme.desc: Alejandro returns home after a terrible accident to discover that he is married to Maria Jose, a poor, innocent girl who was deceived by Alejandro's brother Bruno. Bruno used Alejandro's name to marry Maria Jose, soon after he sent to kill his brother in hopes that Maria Jose would inherit Alejandro's fortune. But when Maria Jose arrives at the mansion she realizes that Bruno lied to her and used her. She is also scared when Alejandro is found alive and returns home. Doctors tell Alejandro that he suffers from memory loss but he is convinced he never met Maria Jose before and goes in search of the truth, but during this time and Maria Jose actually fall in love, while Bruno and Maura (Alejandro's ex-girlfriend) plot to break them up. Meanwhile, the brothers' mother Victoria has fallen in love with Fernando--Alejandro's best friend, so closer to his age than hers.

programme.desc: Alejandro returns home after a terrible accident to discover that he is married to Maria Jose, a poor, innocent girl who was deceived by Alejandro's brother Bruno. Bruno used Alejandro's name to marry Maria Jose, soon after he sent to kill his brother in hopes that Maria Jose would inherit Alejandro's fortune. But when Maria Jose arrives at the mansion she realizes that Bruno lied to her and used her. She is also scared when Alejandro is found alive and returns home. Doctors tell Alejandro that he suffers from memory loss but he is convinced he never met Maria Jose before and goes in search of the truth, but during this time and Maria Jose actually fall in love, while Bruno and Maura (Alejandro's ex-girlfriend) plot to break them up. Meanwhile, the brothers' mother Victoria has fallen in love with Fernando--Alejandro's best friend, so closer to his age than hers.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: After Wednesday befriends a new boy her age, Robespierre Courtney, Morticia invites his parents, Mr. and Mrs. Henry Courtney, to visit the Addams house for tea. Unbeknownst to them, the Courtney's are hoping to meet a number of the social set.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: There is a neighborhood burglar on the loose, and Morticia has reason to believe it could be Gomez. Morticia decides to probe his subconscious mind for a key to his criminality after she and Uncle Fester discover loot hidden in the storeroom.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Morticia's pet plant Cleopatra gobbles up her favorite photo of Gomez from the family album. When the original photographer is found and asked to make a duplicate picture, it is discovered that he is now with the Department of Motor Vehicles.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Gomez plays host to Don Xavier Molines, a family friend during his childhood in Spain, and his daughter, Consuella. Morticia's hospitality is put to the test when Consuella reveals that she has been promised in marriage to Gomez since childhood.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: When Wednesday's and Pugsley's faith in Santa Claus is shaken, Uncle Fester is chosen to back up Santa in case the real St. Nick is too busy to come. However, Fester-Santa gets stuck in the chimney, so each of the other adults fill in for him.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Fester is so smitten upon receipt of a photo of his love, a bearded carnival lady, that he borrows stamp money to mail her a proposal. Morticia dons a beard and poses as the mother to convince Fester that he will have to work to support a wife.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Because she thinks Fester (Jackie Coogan) and Grandmama (Blossom Rock) are spoiling the children, Morticia (Carolyn Jones) hires a governess. Insulted, Fester paints a white line down the center of the Addams house, dividing it in half.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Morticia and Gomez see Fester conferring with TV muscleman Jack LaGrann (Jack LaLanne), and think that Fester is planning a television career. However, Uncle Fester confides to Lurch that he has to go on a secret diet and exercise.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Morticia and Gomez find Grandfather Pegleg's treasure map and summon Captain Grimby. They hope to charter his boat for the treasure hunt. But after meeting the Captain, Morticia is careful to keep the nature of the mission secret.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Ophelia Frump is madly in love with Horatio Bartholomew, the man who has everything, except the truth about her relatives. Morticia, not convinced by Bartholomew, persuades playboy Cousin Itt to stir the embers of his past romance with Ophelia.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Pugsley shocks his parents when he gives up his new atomic reactor as kid stuff and announces that he wants to find his own job. His first try is as a medical assistant to Dr. Bird. He turns up, scalpel in hand, ready to help during an operation.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Grandma Frump (guest star Margaret Hamilton) comes to the mistaken conclusion that her daughter, Morticia (Carolyn Jones), and Gomez (John Astin) plan to pack her off to an old folks home. Actually, they plan to send her to a beauty farm.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Morticia, in order to be part of the National Beautification Program, decides to become a home decorator and offers her services to the neighbors. Next door neighbor, and insurance agent, Joe Digby hires Morticia in hopes of selling them insurance.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Ophelia taunts Uncle Fester into announcing that he is going to join the Peace Corps. Fester feels he's a cinch to be accepted because Gomez plans to pull strings in Washington on his behalf. The entire family agrees to help him study for the exam.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Allyn Joslyn guest-stars as Sam Hilliard, a former truant officer who now heads a private school where Wednesday and Pugsley are enrolled. When Hilliard breaks under the strain of dealing with the Addams children, Gomez buys the school.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Dr. Marvin P. Gunderson is summoned to examine Kitty Kat, the ailing lion pet of the Addams Family. Morticia decides that it is the doctor who needs help. To build his confidence, human members of the family pretend to be ill so he can affect cures.

programme.title: The Addams Family
programme.desc: Morticia's concern that Lurch is overworked leads Gomez to the operating table to assemble a custom-built secondary butler. Lurch lets the robot do all the work and then begins to feel that he isn't needed anymore.

programme.desc: I tested some of the strangest and most unexpected ways people have actually died, recreating different scenarios to see just how real the danger is.

programme.title: I Tested Home Alone Booby Traps
programme.desc: I tested real booby traps inspired by classic movies, engineering and building them myself with my friends to see how dangerous they'd actually be in real life.

programme.title: I Tested "Unbreakable" Products
programme.desc: I put products that claim to be "unbreakable" through extreme tests to see if they can really live up to that promise or if they'll shatter under pressure.

programme.title: 10 Things You Didn't Know Could Kill You
programme.desc: I tested ten surprising things you didn't know could actually kill you, breaking down some common myths to see which ones hold up in real life.

programme.title: I Played GTA With Real Pain
programme.desc: I played GTA 5, Skyrim, Fortnite, and The Forest while wearing a haptic suit that delivers real pain, and the amount of pain it caused genuinely shocked me.

programme.title: I Tested Deadly Weapons From Temu
programme.desc: I bought, unboxed, and tested banned weapons from Temu using ballistic dummies with my friends to see just how dangerous they actually are.

programme.title: I Tested Ai Dogs vs Real Dogs
programme.desc: I bought a real AI robot dog and took it to the dog park to see if it could actually hold its own against real dogs and even replace mine.

programme.title: I Tested 5000 Years of Armor
programme.desc: I tested 5000 years of armor throughout history to see how well it actually holds up against real weapons and attacks.

programme.title: 10 Things You Didn't Know Could Kill You (finale)
programme.desc: I tested 10 more ways you didn't know you could die, including myths like a gate closing on you, a camping tent catching fire, a chandelier falling on you, and a heavy machinery accident.

programme.title: I Tested Deadly Weapons From Anime
programme.desc: I tested deadly anime weapons in real life to see if they actually work, inspired by shows like Demon Slayer, Spy x Family, One Piece, Jujutsu Kaisen, Naruto, and Chainsaw Man.

programme.title: 10 Ways Your House Could Kill You
programme.desc: I tested deadly situations that could happen right inside your own house to see just how dangerous everyday home life can actually be.

programme.title: I Tested Deadly Weapons From Video Games
programme.desc: I tested deadly video game weapons in real life to see if they're actually as effective as they are in the games they come from.

programme.title: I Tested Deadly Home Security Systems
programme.desc: I tested extreme home security devices, including electric door mats, a face-tracking airsoft turret, and a rapid fogging system, to see if they truly protect your home or are just scams.

programme.title: I Tried Escaping Impossible Deaths
programme.desc: I put myself into different deadly situations to see if I could escape in time, like a house fire, quicksand, being locked in a freezer, a straitjacket, a car trunk, and even the back of a police car.

programme.title: I Tested Deadly Island Survival Myths
programme.desc: I tested popular island survival myths to see which ones would actually help you survive and which ones would get you killed.

programme.title: I Tested Movie Deaths In Real Life (again)
programme.desc: I tested movie deaths from popular films in real life again, including a real-life tree cutting scene, to see how accurate they actually are.

programme.title: 10 Sports You Didn't Know Could Kill You (again)
programme.desc: I teamed up with athletes again to showcase dangerous sports impacts and just how much damage they can actually cause.

programme.title: I Tested Brutal Movie Deaths
programme.desc: I tested some of the most brutal movie deaths in real life, including getting hit in the face with a flare, getting stuck in a trash compactor, and having a piano fall on top of me.

programme.title: I Confronted Mack
programme.desc: I finally sat down and asked Mack the questions you guys have been wondering, like what happened to him and whether he'll ever be in another MrBeast video again.

programme.title: I Tested 10,000 Years of Weapons

programme.desc: I tested popular kids toys to see if they're actually as dangerous as everyone says they are.
